etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin antenna, antemna (“yard, sailyard; pole”). First used in this sense as a Latin word in the 15th century and as an English word by the end of the 17th century.

definitions.definition: An appendage used for sensing on the head of an insect, crab, or other animal. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 2006, Timothy Duane Schowalter, Insect Ecology: An Ecosystem Approach, →ISBN, page 22:
quote.text: The overall shape of most insect antennae is elongate and cylindrical, although elaborations into plumose, lamellate, or pectinate forms have arisen many times in different insect lineages.

He put his fingers over his head like two antennas, crossed his eyes, and waggled his tongue like some kind of insect.In the same work, Brown uses antennae to refer to both aerials and feelers during more technical descriptions.

quote.citation: 2010, Craig S. Charron, Daliel J. Cantliffe, "Volatile emissions from plants", Horticultural Reviews, pages 43-72, →ISBN:
quote.text: The basis of these relationships lies in the olfactory chemoreceptors of insect antennas...

definitions.definition: An apparatus to receive or transmit electromagnetic waves and convert respectively to or from an electrical signal.

quote.text: Most nurses believe they are born with an antenna of sorts, which is able to guide them through clinical practice and help them determine what is right and what is not...

quote.citation: 2010, Mary Lou Decostérd, Right Brain/Left Brain President: Barack Obama's Uncommon Leadership Ability, →ISBN, page 106:
quote.text: Obama is astute. He approaches things with the help of a sensitive antenna.

definitions.definition: (nautical) The spar to which a lateen sail is attached, which is then hoisted up the mast.
